findings.title: Staples' forward multiple collapses while trailing stays rich
findings.body: Consumer Staples' forward P/E sits at the 18th percentile of its five-year range even as its trailing multiple remains at the 80th, a 61-point gap that is the widest in the table. The market is pricing a 44 percent earnings jump that has not yet materialized, so the cheapness is a bet on a recovery, not a reflection of current profitability.

findings.title: Materials' extreme gap signals an earnings cliff
findings.body: Materials trades at a 56-point percentile gap between its trailing and forward lenses, with a forward P/E at the 33rd percentile versus trailing at the 89th. That implies a 121 percent earnings surge is expected to rescue the multiple, an unusually aggressive assumption that leaves little room for disappointment.

findings.title: Communication Services is historically cheap on forward earnings
findings.body: Communication Services' forward P/E sits at the 1st percentile of its five-year range, the cheapest any sector gets in this table, while its trailing multiple is only at the 28th. The 57 percent implied earnings growth is already discounted, meaning the market is paying almost nothing for the forward stream and pricing in a steep rebound that must arrive quickly.
